content.text:
All set! The issue was a classic floating-point precision problem. When converting a decimal price to whole cents (by multiplying by 100), JavaScript's floating-point arithmetic produced 3995.0000000000005 instead of 3995 for your 39.95 price.

The fix wraps the multiplication with `Math.round()` in both `parseEuros()` and `cellCents()` functions to ensure the result is always a whole number of cents. Now 39.95 and any other decimal prices will work correctly.
